items.mainDefect: updateDevice treats zero affected rows as ErrDeviceLimitReached, so an existing device whose stored updated_at falls outside the [UpdatedAt-30d, UpdatedAt+1m] window (for example, because of clock skew between HA instances) is wrongly rejected.

secondary.defect: On MySQL, RowsAffected counts changed rows rather than matched rows, so an identical UPDATE on an existing device returns 0 and wrongly triggers ErrDeviceLimitReached.

items.mainDefect: The new updateDevice doc comment says it updates a device 'between the given times', but no times are passed in; the window is computed internally from device.UpdatedAt.

secondary.defect: The updateDevice doc comment does not mention that zero matched rows returns the sentinel ErrDeviceLimitReached, which the auth client depends on.
